I am trying to evaluate which factors influence detection probabilities, such as sex, season, vegetation type...etc.
When I try to add season as a temporal covariate using timecov and fit a model, I get only NA values for all parameters. I cannot figure out if the problem comes from the data input or something else.
Does anyone have any idea?

Many thanks in advance,
Sophie

parts:
Hi Anne-Sophie
I mocked up a simple analogue of your analysis and it seemed to work:
library(secr)
CH <- ovenCHp[[1]]
msk <- make.mask(traps(CH), buffer = 300, nx = 20, type = 'trapbuffer')
timecovs <- data.frame(occasion = 1:9, season = factor(rep(1:3, each = 3)))
fit <- secr.fit(CH, timecov = timecovs, model = list(D~1, sigma~season),
                hcov = 'Sex', mask = msk)
That leaves me scratching my head. I note a couple of small glitches in your code - specifying 'buffer' has no effect if you specify 'mask' directly, and D~1 is not compatible with CL = T, but these don't explain the failure of the model to fit.
Maybe the problem is in the initial parameter values.
Murray

Hi Murray,

thank you for your answer, I changed CL = T for CL = F.
I found out that there was an issue with hcov. I am using a trap usage, and as you explained in this thread (http://www.phidot.org/forum/viewtopic.php?f=36&t=2069), when the first camera is not used on the first occasion, it causes mixture models to fail. The model is now working without specifying starting values.

Anne-Sophie
